decisions.decision: Deviated from the roadmap tier table's literal 'via clock.LoadOrDefault': config substitutes the default BEFORE resolution instead of passing the env value through LoadOrDefault.
decisions.why: LoadOrDefault("") returns UTC, not Bogota — time.LoadLocation special-cases "" with no error, so the fallback never fires. The literal shorthand would have produced a silent UTC poller.

decisions.decision: No zone-name constant added to internal/clock; config calls clock.Zone().String().
decisions.why: Zone().String() reads the same computed value Zone() uses. A parallel constant would be a second source of truth for the same string — over-abstraction, which CLAUDE.md's AI-efficiency rule warns against.

decisions.why: Leader verified both against README:205 and the graph block. This is the docs-track-structural-change rule, which ai/agentic-workflow.md names as changes-requested, not a nit. Leader missed it in its own T5 pass.

findings.note: README.md:205 and README.md:238 (dependency graph LAYER 0 line) are now stale. Line 205 states internal/clock is 'not yet adopted by any other module' — false as of this tier, config adopts it. Line 238's LAYER 0 leaf list ('tesla googleauth auth config testdb <module>/db') still shows config with no internal dependencies, but config now imports internal/clock. CLAUDE.md's docs-track-structural-change rule (restated in ai/agentic-workflow.md's reviewer-role section as 'not a nit') requires the README architecture/dependency-graph docs to be updated in the SAME change when a module's public surface/dependency set changes. Fix: move config off the LAYER 0 depends-on-nothing line into a line showing config → clock, and update clock's row to drop 'not yet adopted by any other module' (or state it is now adopted by config).

Re-verified against 0386b5a (README.md only, zero Go/code change; progress.json D20 records the fix). clock's row (README.md:205) no longer claims non-adoption — now states config adopted it in tier 2 and names tiers 3-6. Graph's LAYER 0 line no longer lists config as dependency-free; config now sits under a relabeled 'LAYER 1 — domain modules & config' header with an explicit `config → clock` arrow, and clock was added to the LAYER 0 leaves line. Confirmed independently: (a) clock imports stdlib time only (re-read clock.go), so LAYER 0's own definition ('no internal dependencies') genuinely holds for it — correct placement, consistent with how tesla/auth/testdb (also imported by higher layers) already sit on that same line; the graph's layer number reflects each package's own dependency depth, not who imports it. (b) config's placement under 'domain modules & config' is topologically accurate (config's only internal dependency, clock, is a LAYER-0 leaf — same depth as telemetry/charging/account, which depend only on LAYER-0 adapters + their own db packages) and the header's explicit '& config' phrasing does not claim config IS a domain module — it flags them as two distinct categories sharing a depth tier. This is a legitimate stylistic choice, not a factual misrepresentation; no restructure required. Confirmed no other file touched (`git diff 0386b5a~1 0386b5a --stat`: README.md + this change's own progress.json only), `git status --porcelain` clean, `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` both pass. R1 fixed.
